question: ‘Roads to Mussoorie’, the famous novel is written by whom among the following Sahitya Akademi Awardee?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ruskin Bond**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ruskin Bond** is a celebrated Indian author of British descent.
 
• He received the **Sahitya Akademi Award in 1992** for his novel "Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra".
 
• "Roads to Mussoorie" is one of his notable works, highlighting his life experiences and observations in Mussoorie, a hill station in India.
 
• Bond's writing often reflects his deep connection with nature and the simple life of the hills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sahitya Akademi Award**

 
 
• It is a literary honor in India, which the Sahitya Akademi, India's National Academy of Letters, annually confers on writers of outstanding works in one of the twenty-four major Indian languages.
 
• Established in 1954, it is one of the most prestigious literary awards in India.
 
• The award includes a plaque and a cash prize.
 
 
 
• **Mussoorie**
 
 
• A hill station in the Dehradun District of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• Known for its scenic beauty and pleasant weather, it is also referred to as the "Queen of the Hills".
 
• It has been a popular destination for tourists and writers alike.
 
 
 
• **Ruskin Bond's Literary Contributions**
 
 
• Bond has written over 500 short stories, essays, and novels.
 
• His works are known for their simplicity and depth, often capturing the essence of life in the Indian hills.
 
• Some of his other notable works include "The Room on the Roof" and "The Blue Umbrella".
